fixes.explanation: Thank is it. Paul writes, "We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you…" (Colossians 1:3). Notice the word always. Nobody's tapping a watch here, because thanking God goes along with every time they pray for the Colossians.

Paul doesn't say they question God. He says, "We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you…" (Colossians 1:3). Every time they pray for the Colossians, thanking God is part of it. Thanks is the word.

Remind is a fair guess, since a lot of us treat prayer like a to-do list. But Paul says, "We always thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, when we pray for you…" (Colossians 1:3). The word is thank.
In heaven, baker. Paul calls it "…the hope stored up for you in heaven…" (Colossians 1:5). It's kept up there, and that's a storage unit I'd trust.

Epaphras it is. Paul says, "You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant…" (Colossians 1:7). He's also called a faithful minister of Christ on Paul's behalf. I started out in a bakery bin with a 25 cent price sticker on me, so I'd take a title like that any day.

Barnabas is a familiar name, but he isn't the one in this verse. Paul says, "You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant…" (Colossians 1:7). So the Colossians heard the gospel from Epaphras. Good guess on a familiar name, though.
Silas is a familiar name, but he isn't named here. Paul says, "You learned it from Epaphras, our beloved fellow servant…" (Colossians 1:7). Epaphras is the one the Colossians learned it from.
Spirit, yes. Paul says Epaphras "…also informed us of your love in the Spirit." (Colossians 1:8). Epaphras told Paul and Timothy about that love. A good report is a gift.

Church seems like a safe guess, but Paul words it differently. He says Epaphras "…informed us of your love in the Spirit." (Colossians 1:8). Paul names the Spirit as where their love is. That's the word he picked.

Prophecy sounds like a big thing to ask for, but it isn't what Paul asks for here. He prays that God would "…fill you with the knowledge of His will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding…" (Colossians 1:9). So the answer is the knowledge of His will.

Paul doesn't put it that way. He says the knowledge is "…so that you may walk in a manner worthy of the Lord and may please Him in every way…" (Colossians 1:10). Then he goes on, "…bearing fruit in every good work, growing in the knowledge of God…" (Colossians 1:10). That's a life being lived, and nothing there says they're earning anything.

Signs and wonders sound exciting, but Paul doesn't ask for them here. He prays they'll be "…strengthened with all power according to His glorious might so that you may have full endurance and patience…" (Colossians 1:11). So the answer is endurance and patience.
True. Paul says the Father "…has qualified you to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light." (Colossians 1:12). Notice who does the qualifying: the Father.

Darkness, baker. Paul says, "He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son…" (Colossians 1:13). Rescued out and brought in. I spent years in the dark at the back of a junk drawer before I was called out, and being pulled out of the dark never gets old.

Egypt is a real place, but it isn't the word here. Paul says, "He has rescued us from the dominion of darkness and brought us into the kingdom of His beloved Son…" (Colossians 1:13). The blank is darkness.

Record is a tricky one, but Paul doesn't say it. He writes, "…in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins." (Colossians 1:14). Paul says redemption is the forgiveness of sins, so a record of them isn't what he points to. The word is forgiveness.
